incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 - Traffic spike and connection resets observed for ALB target group in eu-west-1a. 5xx rate up ~18%. Paging #eng-oncall and #eng-networking.

Miguel (oncall): Received the page, jumping in. Any immediate customer-facing symptoms?

Nadia (support): Several customers reporting intermittent timeouts and 502s from the API gateway since ~10:02 UTC. Ticket count up 32 in the last 10 minutes.

Priya (networking): Seeing target_health=unhealthy for ~40% of targets in TG:rgw-api-eu-west-1. The failing targets are concentrated in eu-west-1a. Health check failures show connection reset / upstream closed.

Erin (eng-sre): Correlating with Envoy logs on those instances — lots of RST_STREAM and downstream reset 0x1. Upstream to the model pods shows 504s at the instance level.

Miguel (oncall): Steps I'm taking now: 1) Drain targets in eu-west-1a from the ALB target group, 2) Temporarily mark AZ as out-of-service in autoscaling routing, 3) Increase connection timeout in Envoy to avoid premature resets while we diagnose.

Priya (networking): Agree with draining. I'm also seeing a small spike in control-plane errors to ASG that looks like recent rolling updates finished at ~09:58 UTC. Could be a bad image or liveness probe change.

Jordan (platform): Logs from the deploy pipeline show a deployment to eu-west-1a at 09:56 with a new sidecar commit (rev g7f2). I'll pull the container logs.

deploy-bot: Deployment g7f2 completed to eu-west-1a for service rgw-proxy at 09:56:23 UTC.

Priya (networking): While Miguel drains the targets, I can route ALB weight to eu-west-1b/c via traffic-split. DNS TTLs are 60s; lowering won't help immediate routing but traffic-split at ALB or Route53 weighted records can help.

Miguel (oncall): Executed: 
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:...:targetgroup/rgw-api/abcd1234 --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h,Id=i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a
```
Targets are draining now. Health in other AZs stable. 5xx rate dropping to ~6%

Nadia (support): Tickets slowing but still trickling. Customers seeing degraded throughput but not complete failure. Notifying enterprise customers on the watchlist.

Erin (eng-sre): Captured Envoy snippet showing resets: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:10Z] envoy error: stream_id=45324 upstream_reset:reason=connection_failure upstream_host=10.0.13.12:8080
```
Upstream pod 10.0.13.12 shows oom_kill in kernel logs around same time. Looks like a resource issue not ALB itself.

Miguel (oncall): If upstream OOMs are happening, draining AZ buys us time. I'll also scale up the pods in eu-west-1b/c to absorb traffic. Triggering a scale + temporarily increase pod memory limit? Need approval.

Priya (networking): Scaling is fine. Also changing ALB target group deregistration delay shorter to speed failover: set to 30s (was 300s).

Jordan (platform): Scaling launch looks good; new pods becoming Ready in eu-west-1b/c.

Miguel (oncall): Made the deregistration change: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30`

Practical note: Adjusting deregistration delay improves failover speed but may drop in-flight requests. We reduced to 30s since customers are already impacted.

Priya (networking): I will also add a temporary listener rule to prefer AZs b,c via target group weighting to encourage cross-AZ distribution at the ALB level.

Erin (eng-sre): Confirming 5xx now back under 2% after drains and scale. Customers report improved connectivity.

Nadia (support): Sending status update to affected customers: "Partial degradation in EU region resolved; still monitoring."

Miguel (oncall): Root cause hypothesis: recent sidecar change (g7f2) introduced a memory regression causing pod OOMs under steady traffic in eu-west-1a. Autoscaling didn't replace instances fast enough, ALB kept routing to unhealthy targets, causing Envoy upstream resets and user-facing 502/504.

Priya (networking): Short-term mitigation done. Next steps: rollback sidecar in eu-west-1a to previous stable (g7e9) and run canary with reduced concurrency. Also patch ASG healthcheck thresholds to catch the regressions faster.

Jordan (platform): I'll prepare rollback PR and a controlled rollout plan. Will also add an ASG lifecycle hook to cordon bad instances quicker.

Miguel (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm going to stay on incident until rollback completes. After rollback and stability for 30m, we'll de-escalate to SEV3 and assign follow-up.

Erin (eng-sre): Add to action items: 
- Rollback g7f2 in eu-west-1a (Jordan)
- Run memory profiling on sidecar image (Erin)
- Postmortem with timeline and customer impact (Miguel + Nadia)
- Update ALB deregistration delay and ASG healthcheck docs (Priya)

Nadia (support): I'll consolidate impacted customer list and prepare templates for post-incident outreach.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation: targets drained in eu-west-1a, traffic shifted to eu-west-1b/c, pods scaled. 5xx reduced. Paging cleared for now.

Miguel (oncall): Rolling back sidecar in eu-west-1a now. Command: 
```
kubectl -n services set image deployment/rgw-proxy rgw-proxy=registry/redwood/rgw-proxy:g7e9 --record
```

Jordan (platform): Rollback applied; monitoring rollout.

Erin (eng-sre): Post-rollback checks: memory stable, no OOMs in last 5m, Envoy resets stop. 5xx baseline normal.

Nadia (support): Customers updated: outage mitigated; preparing a follow-up message with root cause and compensatory measures.

Miguel (oncall): Closing active pager. We'll keep an incident thread open for the postmortem and exactly when we changed configurations. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Jordan (platform): Quick note for postmortem: include timestamps for ASG events and deregistration_delay change.

Priya (networking): Also include ALB request count per AZ and per-target metrics.

Erin (eng-sre): I'll collect Envoy and kernel logs and attach samples.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to post-incident review. Severity downgraded to SEV3.

Miguel (oncall): Final action items assigned in ticket INC-20260315-007. We'll sync in the 11:30 postmortem.
